pathway.title: Brightstar Lottery PLC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Reported leverage is the figure to anchor on, and it has risen. Net debt of USD 3,796 million was 4.72x reported EBITDA at June 2026 against 3.94x at year-end 2025 (4.73x and 4.77x pro forma for the July 31 repurchases and September 1 dividend, with the July 10 tax payment effect not established), because the final Italian Lotto installment was paid in cash. Management's 3.24x adds back USD 201 million of license fee amortization, 35% of first-half adjusted EBITDA, for cash that was paid up front, so creditors should read the higher figure as the working measure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 12; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05

- Business quality is strong and gives visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts with government lotteries, the main contracts have more than five years left on average, and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034. That durability helps support leverage above 4x on a reported basis; it weakens only where one regulator controls the license. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40, 41

- Liquidity and maturities are not the pressure point. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million at June 2026 is 1.70 times the USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028, and nothing is due in the rest of 2026, so a refinancing could wait for the outlook to be proved. The drawn revolver of USD 604 million and 40% floating-rate debt do raise interest sensitivity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C03; calculation C04

- Cash generation after minority distributions and payouts is the weakest link. In the first half free cash flow excluding the Lotto payment was USD 269 million, distributions to minority partners took USD 194 million, leaving USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. Management's outlook implies second-half free cash flow before any distributions of only USD 6 million to USD 31 million, so net debt is unlikely to fall in 2026 without lower payouts or partner funding. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7; calculation C06; calculation C08

- License concentration is the main business risk. The two Italian licenses supply 37% of revenue; the Scratch & Win license, 19% of revenue, expires in September 2028 and is stated to be non-renewable, so its replacement lands in the same year as the first large note maturity. The filings give no renewal timetable or terms. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40; calculation C05

- Control and financial policy are a medium risk. One shareholder holds 63.28% of votes, there is no formal dividend policy and payouts continued during the license payment, but eight of thirteen directors are independent and earlier financing agreements capped payouts by rating level; whether the March 2026 revolving agreement does the same is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 171, 175

- Currency mismatch is a secondary risk. Euro debt is 66% of principal while Italy supplies about 40% of revenue, so a stronger euro raises the dollar value of debt faster than earnings, although half of cash is also in euros. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C09

runs.text: The main strength is contract visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts with government lotteries, fees follow wagers and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, so revenue is more predictable than in most consumer businesses and supports tolerance for leverage above 4x on a reported basis. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million against USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028 adds a second strength, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.19x. The main weaknesses are leverage and cash after distributions. Reported net leverage rose to 4.72x after the final Lotto payment, management's lower figure rests on adding back license amortization, and after USD 194 million paid to minority partners the first-half cash left was USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. License concentration, a 63.28% controlling holder and 40% floating-rate debt add to the risk; each is explained in the key findings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 40; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C06

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The company sold its gaming and digital business to a holding company owned by Apollo funds on July 1, 2025 for USD 4.1 billion net of cash transferred, repaid USD 2,936 million of principal during 2025, and returned USD 1,041 million to shareholders in 2025. It won the nine-year Italian Lotto license, paid the EUR 2.23 billion fee in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and had partners fund 38.5% of the final installment. New debt in the period was a EUR 1 billion term loan due 2030 (March 2025), USD 750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due 2033 (December 2025) that refinanced the 6.250% notes due 2027, and new revolving facilities of USD 650 million and EUR 1.0 billion due March 2031 (agreement March 2026, effective April 2026). The 2026 notes were redeemed in September 2025. Basis: 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 15, 17; 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 139, 163, 169–170; 6-K_2025-09-30_brightstar-9302025xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation C01; calculation C09

fields.value: Liquidity fell to USD 1,742 million from USD 3,036 million as cash dropped to USD 558 million, and 50% of the cash is in euros. No maturity falls due in the rest of 2026, USD 228 million falls due in 2027 and USD 798 million in 2028, so near-term refinancing risk is limited; the drawn revolver of USD 604 million is due in 2031. Floating-rate debt rose to 40% of the total from 36% and 25% at the two previous year-ends, and no interest rate swaps were held at the end of 2025, so interest cost is more sensitive to euro rates.

A pause in factoring would lower operating cash flow and raise reported receivables and debt needs, so factoring volumes and the collected-on-behalf balance are worth tracking beside leverage.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that cover and liquidity remain adequate, no maturity falls due before 2027, and management reaffirms its full-year outlook and expects free cash flow to rise after the 2025 to 2028 capital expenditure cycle. That view would win if reported net leverage falls back toward the 3.94x of year-end 2025 as the Lotto cash cost drops out of operating cash flow and minority partners keep funding their share; it would lose if the next report shows net debt above USD 3,848 million, the June figure plus the July repurchases and the September dividend, with no earnings growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is contract-based and long-dated but concentrated in two government licenses. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts, and the two Italian licenses that one regulator awards supply 37% of revenue, so a loss or non-renewal there would cut cash flow far more than any single United States contract.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Scratch & Win license, 19% of revenue, expires in September 2028 and is stated to be non-renewable, so its replacement is decided by a new award whose conditions the law will set. That date falls in the same year as the first large note maturity, so refinancing and license renewal risk coincide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Lotto license, effective December 2025 for nine years, is now secured, but its USD 2,601 million upfront cost was paid in cash and amortizes against revenue for years. Partners funded 38.5% of the final installment through a capital increase, which limits the group's own cash call but means minority holders take a large share of the license's profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 6-K_2026-03-31_brightstar-3312026xform6k.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12; calculation C02; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with one shareholder: De Agostini holds 46.29% of the ordinary shares but 63.28% of the votes through the loyalty voting structure, appoints an observer to the board and has executives on it, so payout, financing and merger decisions are effectively its to approve. No sponsor-style willingness evidence exists beyond the documented actions in the registers below, and legal capacity for distributions is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation has tilted toward shareholders: the 2025 special dividend and accelerated repurchase alone were USD 859 million, the regular dividend rose from USD 0.20 to USD 0.23 per share, and USD 186 million of the repurchase program remains, while the company states no formal dividend policy. Creditors are protected mainly by contractual limits and the debt reduction that followed the sale, which this analysis cannot size without the financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 171, 182–183; 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C06; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Structure leaves creditors secured by the shares of the Italian operating subsidiary, with the parent, the Dutch holding company and a US co-issuer as issuers and guarantors of different instruments, and consortium partners owning part of the licensed operating companies. Cash held in the joint ventures is shared with minority partners through dividends of USD 163 million in each of the first halves of 2025 and 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Overall sponsor and governance risk is medium: control and payout discretion are high, but disclosure is detailed, eight of thirteen directors are independent, related-party dealings with the controlling holder are small and the outstanding distribution limits are tied to credit ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is the durability of the contracts: the revenue-weighted remaining term of the main contracts is more than five years, the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, 15 platform customers and nearly 90 lottery customers diversify the rest, and the debt reduction and covenant-protected distribution limits after the sale reduce the chance of debt-funded payouts. The view would soften if the Scratch & Win license is extended or replaced on similar terms before 2028, or if the 2026 revolving agreement is shown to carry tight payout limits. It would harden if shareholder returns resume above free cash flow after minority distributions, if a license is lost or renewed on worse terms, or if the controlling holder uses its voting power to approve a debt-funded distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The terms of the revolving credit agreement signed in March 2026 on distributions, guarantor coverage and security are not stated, so the conclusion that shareholder payouts are contractually limited rests on the earlier agreements' terms and may be wrong for today's facilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The significant subsidiaries exhibit and the organization chart were not in the supplied text, so ownership percentages below the parent for most operating companies are not established, which limits the conclusion about where creditor collateral and guarantees reach.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contract-level data such as expiry dates for the largest United States contracts, renewal options and termination compensation are given only as weighted averages, so the durability conclusion is an average and a single large expiry could change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The customer behind the 37% share is not named in the passage on concentration; the match to the Italian regulator rests on the two licenses' shares adding to the same figure, an analyst reading that would be wrong if another customer is meant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company sold its gaming and digital business to a holding company owned by Apollo funds on July 1, 2025 for USD 4.1 billion net of cash transferred, repaid USD 2,936 million of principal during 2025, and returned USD 1,041 million to shareholders in 2025. It won the nine-year Italian Lotto license, paid the EUR 2.23 billion fee in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and had partners fund 38.5% of the final installment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in the period was a EUR 1 billion term loan due 2030 (March 2025), USD 750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due 2033 (December 2025) that refinanced the 6.250% notes due 2027, and new revolving facilities of USD 650 million and EUR 1.0 billion due March 2031 (agreement March 2026, effective April 2026). The 2026 notes were redeemed in September 2025.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Brightstar Lottery PLC as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is business quality, cash generation, liquidity, leverage, refinancing, ownership and financial policy, built on the supplied financial foundation and business analysis, with a qualitative downside path and monitoring triggers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used. Document dates are the signature dates the documents state; the three presentations state none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Brightstar's credit is solid on business quality but stretched on cash after the Italian Lotto payment: reported net leverage of 4.72x is well above management's 3.24x, and with distributions continuing, creditors depend on free cash flow recovering as license payments end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At June 2026 reported net leverage was 4.72x, or 4.73x pro forma for the July 31, 2026 repurchases and 4.77x pro forma for the dividend payable September 1, 2026; the effect of the July 10, 2026 tax settlement payment is not established. Liquidity and maturities leave room to wait for that recovery, but management's own outlook implies thin second-half free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported leverage is the figure to anchor on, and it has risen. Net debt of USD 3,796 million was 4.72x reported EBITDA at June 2026 against 3.94x at year-end 2025 (4.73x and 4.77x pro forma for the July 31 repurchases and September 1 dividend, with the July 10 tax payment effect not established), because the final Italian Lotto installment was paid in cash. Management's 3.24x adds back USD 201 million of license fee amortization, 35% of first-half adjusted EBITDA, for cash that was paid up front, so creditors should read the higher figure as the working measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 12; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business quality is strong and gives visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts with government lotteries, the main contracts have more than five years left on average, and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034. That durability helps support leverage above 4x on a reported basis; it weakens only where one regulator controls the license.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and maturities are not the pressure point. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million at June 2026 is 1.70 times the USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028, and nothing is due in the rest of 2026, so a refinancing could wait for the outlook to be proved. The drawn revolver of USD 604 million and 40% floating-rate debt do raise interest sensitivity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C03; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation after minority distributions and payouts is the weakest link. In the first half free cash flow excluding the Lotto payment was USD 269 million, distributions to minority partners took USD 194 million, leaving USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. Management's outlook implies second-half free cash flow before any distributions of only USD 6 million to USD 31 million, so net debt is unlikely to fall in 2026 without lower payouts or partner funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.2_2026-06-30_q226earningsslidedeck-fi.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7; calculation C06; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - License concentration is the main business risk. The two Italian licenses supply 37% of revenue; the Scratch & Win license, 19% of revenue, expires in September 2028 and is stated to be non-renewable, so its replacement lands in the same year as the first large note maturity. The filings give no renewal timetable or terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 20-F_2025-12-31_igt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 40; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control and financial policy are a medium risk. One shareholder holds 63.28% of votes, there is no formal dividend policy and payouts continued during the license payment, but eight of thirteen directors are independent and earlier financing agreements capped payouts by rating level; whether the March 2026 revolving agreement does the same is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Currency mismatch is a secondary risk. Euro debt is 66% of principal while Italy supplies about 40% of revenue, so a stronger euro raises the dollar value of debt faster than earnings, although half of cash is also in euros.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K_2026-06-30_brightstar-6302026xform6k.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 27; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that the leverage jump reflects a one-off license payment that partners funded in part, that management reaffirms an adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 1.16 billion to USD 1.19 billion with operating cash flow before license payments near USD 750 million, and that it expects free cash flow above USD 400 million a year after the 2025 to 2028 spending cycle. The view would soften if second-half cash flow beats the implied USD 6 million to USD 31 million, if the Scratch & Win renewal is secured early, or if payouts are cut. It would harden if reported net leverage stays above 4.77x at the next report, if the revolver is drawn to fund distributions, or if the Italian regulator signals a less favorable replacement license.

fields.value: - The outlook figures are management's and the second-half arithmetic subtracts first-half actuals from full-year ranges, so the conclusion that second-half cash flow will not cover payouts could reverse if working capital unwinds after the first-half timing drag the company describes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strength is contract visibility. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term operating contracts with government lotteries, fees follow wagers and the Italian Lotto license now runs to 2034, so revenue is more predictable than in most consumer businesses and supports tolerance for leverage above 4x on a reported basis. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million against USD 1,026 million due in 2027 and 2028 adds a second strength, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.19x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are leverage and cash after distributions. Reported net leverage rose to 4.72x after the final Lotto payment, management's lower figure rests on adding back license amortization, and after USD 194 million paid to minority partners the first-half cash left was USD 75 million against USD 130 million of dividends and buybacks. License concentration, a 63.28% controlling holder and 40% floating-rate debt add to the risk; each is explained in the key findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A credible downside begins with the Italian regulator's replacement award for the Scratch & Win license in 2028, or an earlier United States jackpot drought. The first operational break would be lower service revenue at fixed amortization and equipment costs, which cuts reported EBITDA faster than revenue because fees are percentages of wagers and cost is largely fixed. Higher reported leverage and lower cover follow, and distributions to minority partners and shareholders would continue unless cut, so cash after payouts would turn negative and the revolver would fund the gap. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million would absorb a year of that, but the 2028 maturities of USD 798 million then fall due with weaker earnings, which is when refinancing cost or access becomes the issue. Observable triggers are in the monitoring register: reported leverage above its pro forma level, second-half free cash flow below the implied range, and any renewal news.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management reaffirmed its full-year outlook on August 4, 2026: revenue of USD 2.50 billion to USD 2.55 billion, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.16 billion to USD 1.19 billion, capital expenditure of USD 450 million to USD 475 million and operating cash flow of about USD 750 million before license payments. The adjusted EBITDA range implies USD 587 million to USD 617 million in the second half against USD 597 million a year earlier, so the outlook is roughly flat after the first half. Tailwinds are digital growth, cost savings of about USD 100 million by 2028 and the end of license payments; headwinds are higher license amortization, a growth investment of about USD 50 million in 2026 and jackpot volatility.
